title: RedLab Campaign
description: A declarative, portable adversarial-test campaign. RedLab is the content standard; an execution runtime (AROS) reads this file, runs it under policy in a sandbox, and emits an evidence bundle. A campaign is a falsifiable security claim plus everything needed to attack it and to believe or disbelieve the result.

id.description: Stable slug, unique across all projects. e.g. dycrpt-replay-resistance

target.description: Which project and exact revision this campaign is written against. revision_pin makes a result reproducible and lets RedLab detect when the surface moved under it.

revision_pin.description: commit SHA the campaign was authored against

historical_pattern.description: The real-world failure lineage this campaign guards against. Grounds the test in something that has actually broken before, in this class of system.

surface.description: The concrete, per-project attack surface: the exact functions/files/FFI boundary the attacker touches. This is what makes a campaign portable-by-instantiation rather than portable-in-theory.

invariant.description: The security hypothesis, stated so it can be FALSIFIED. 'X can never happen'. The oracle exists to try to make X happen.

attacker_capabilities.description: What the adversary is assumed to control (e.g. 'can capture and replay ciphertexts', 'can supply arbitrary bytes to the parser'). No capability = no threat model = not a campaign.

prerequisites.description: State that must hold before the attack is meaningful (e.g. 'an established session', 'at least one delivered message').

resource_limits.description: Hard bounds the runtime enforces. A campaign that cannot bound its own cost cannot be run under containment.

assigned_roles.description: Which agent roles (see agents/roles.json) drive this campaign.

generator.description: How the adversarial input/harness is produced and run. 'command' runs INSIDE the sandbox against the pinned target.

oracle.description: The pass/fail judge. success_means = attacker succeeded = invariant BROKEN = campaign FAILS. The oracle observes the target's real behaviour; it must never key its verdict off a label.

success_means.description: condition under which the ATTACK succeeded

negative_control.description: a condition that MUST NOT trigger success, to catch a tautological oracle

expected_outcome.description: What we EXPECT today. A hardened target expects invariant_holds; a known-vulnerable fixture expects invariant_broken. Divergence from expectation is the finding.

required_evidence.description: The evidence levels a result must reach to be believed. E4 = independent reproduction on a fresh instance of the exact target; E7 = re-attack of the patched twin + regression.

severity_rationale.description: Why this matters if the invariant breaks. Written before the run, so severity is not rationalized after the fact.
